sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is a special episode of The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》的一期特别节目。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, we introduced a series focused on what a second Trump presidency would look like and how it would challenge democratic norMs.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，我们推出了一系列节目，重点探讨特朗普第二次总统任期会是什么样子，以及它将如何挑战民主规范。

sentences.en: We documented Trump's plans to consolidate power by firing federal workers who would stand in his way, taking control of federal agencies that have long operated independently,
sentences.zh: 我们记录了特朗普巩固权力的计划：解雇那些会阻挠他的联邦雇员，接管长期独立运作的联邦机构，

sentences.en: and using the powers of a government to seek revenge against his enemies.
sentences.zh: 并利用政府权力向他的敌人寻求报复。

sentences.en: Today, we look more closely at Trump's growing plans for revenge, which are often dismissed as mere bluster by his allies and supporters.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们更近距离地审视特朗普不断升级的复仇计划，这些计划经常被他的盟友和支持者斥为虚张声势。

sentences.en: But new reporting from my colleague, Mike Schmidt, shows that it's far from bluster.
sentences.zh: 但我的同事迈克·施密特的新报道表明，这绝非虚张声势。

sentences.en: Because as Mike found, when Trump asked for retribution in his first term,
sentences.zh: 因为正如迈克所发现的，当特朗普在第一任期内要求报复时，

sentences.en: Mike, as you know, we have been working on a series about what a second Trump presidency would look like.
sentences.zh: 迈克，如你所知，我们一直在制作一个关于特朗普第二任期会是什么样子的系列节目。

sentences.en: And inevitably, in thinking about this series, we went to you to ask you for your thoughts, as somebody who covered the first Trump term so closely.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，在构思这个系列时，我们找到了你，向你征求意见，因为你曾如此密切地报道过特朗普的第一任期。

sentences.en: And you encouraged us to linger a little bit longer on a question we have started to broach, which is the question of retribution and how central that would be to a second term.
sentences.zh: 你鼓励我们在一个我们已经开始触及的问题上多停留一会儿，那就是复仇的问题，以及这对于第二任期会有多核心。

sentences.en: Why do you think we need to focus on the idea of retribution?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么我们需要关注复仇这个概念？

sentences.en: I think this is the most important issue about Trump and what he could do if he returns to the White House.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是关于特朗普以及他如果重返白宫会做什么的最重要问题。

sentences.en: And here's why.
sentences.zh: 原因如下。

sentences.en: I don't think that the issue has been properly framed in the public's mind.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个问题在公众心目中还没有得到正确的界定。

sentences.en: I will appoint a real special prosecutor to go after the most corrupt president in the history of the United States of America,
sentences.zh: 我将任命一名真正的特别检察官，去追查美国历史上最腐败的总统，

sentences.en: when Trump goes out and says he's going to come back and use the sacred powers of the federal government against his enemies.
sentences.zh: 当特朗普公开说他要卷土重来，并动用联邦政府的神圣权力来对付他的政敌时，

sentences.en: And all others involved with the destruction of our elections, our borders and our country itself, they're destroying our country.
sentences.zh: 以及所有其他参与破坏我们选举、我们的边境和我们国家本身的人，他们在毁灭我们的国家。

sentences.en: And his allies say,
sentences.zh: 他的盟友们说，

sentences.en: Donald Trump has been the one that's been very clear that his vengeance is going to be by winning and making America great again, not going after his political opponents.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普一直非常明确地表示，他的复仇方式将是通过赢得胜利并让美国再次伟大，而不是去追查他的政治对手。

sentences.en: He said that.
sentences.zh: 他是这么说的。

sentences.en: This is just bluster, right?
sentences.zh: 这只是虚张声势，对吧？

sentences.en: All he's suggesting is that we should investigate credible arguments of wrongdoing.
sentences.zh: 他所暗示的全部内容就是我们应该调查那些关于不当行为的可信论点。

sentences.en: That's all that Donald Trump is saying.
sentences.zh: 这就是唐纳德·特朗普所说的全部内容。

sentences.en: That is not a threat to democracy.
sentences.zh: 这并不是对民主的威胁。

sentences.en: That's merely reinforcing our system of law and government.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是在巩固我们的法律和政府体系。

sentences.en: And candidly, I think that the news media has treated this as a hypothetical as well.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我认为新闻媒体也将此视作一种假设。

sentences.en: The media says if Trump comes back, he says he's going to seek retribution.
sentences.zh: 媒体说，如果特朗普卷土重来，他说他将寻求复仇。

sentences.en: This is a warning about what Trump may do.
sentences.zh: 这是对特朗普可能会做什么的警告。

sentences.en: Well, what's insufficient about that?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种说法有什么不足之处呢？

sentences.en: What's insufficient about that is that he already did this.
sentences.zh: 这种说法的不足之处在于，他已经这么做过了。

sentences.en: He did this when he was president.
sentences.zh: 他在当总统的时候就这么做过。

sentences.en: And he did it to a degree far greater than even I, someone who's been trying to cover this since the moment he came into the White House, appreciated.
sentences.zh: 而且他这样做的时候，其程度甚至远远超出了我的想象——我可是一个从他入主白宫那一刻起就一直试图报道这一点的人。

sentences.en: He was actually much more successful when he was president in weaponizing the government against his enemies.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当他担任总统时，他在将政府武器化以对付政敌方面取得了更大的成功。

sentences.en: Well, just explain what you mean when you say he's already done this to a degree that you yourself didn't even appreciate in real time.
sentences.zh: 那么，请解释一下你所说的“他在当时甚至连你自己都没有意识到的大程度上已经这么做过了”是什么意思。

sentences.en: So I spent the past several months looking back at his presidency, going through my notes,
sentences.zh: 所以我过去几个月一直在回顾他的总统任期，翻阅我的笔记，

sentences.en: going through documents that I had, looking at court filings, interviewing a range of people.
sentences.zh: 翻阅我拥有的文件，查看法庭文件，采访了形形色色的人。

sentences.en: And what I found was that there were nearly a dozen instances in which something that Trump
sentences.zh: 我发现，有近十起事件表明，特朗普

sentences.en: wanted done with the powers of the government, with the powers of the Justice Department, the FBI, or the IRS, were actually done to his enemies.
sentences.zh: 想要利用政府权力、司法部、联邦调查局或国税局的权力去办的事，真的被用到了他的政敌身上。

sentences.en: And here's why I think this is so important.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为这如此重要。

sentences.en: Trump engaged in a range of questionable conduct when he was president.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在任总统期间进行了一系列可疑的行为。

sentences.en: But I think there's something really distinct about this type of behavior.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这种类型的行为确实有其独特之处。

sentences.en: Which is what?
sentences.zh: 什么独特之处？

sentences.en: If Trump is going to weaponize the government against his enemies, it starts to head the country down the path of authoritarianism.
sentences.zh: 如果特朗普要将政府武器化来对付政敌，这就开始让国家走向独裁主义的道路。

sentences.en: That's a really big word.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大的词。

sentences.en: So I want you to justify using it.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你证明使用这个词是合理的。

sentences.en: The government is supposed to use its vast powers
sentences.zh: 政府本应利用其庞大的权力

sentences.en: to prosecute cases based on the facts and the law.
sentences.zh: 根据事实和法律来起诉案件。

sentences.en: But when those powers are used against individuals for reasons not based on the facts and the law, but based on the whims of a politician, the president of the United States,
sentences.zh: 但当这些权力被用来对付个人，其原因不是基于事实和法律，而是基于一个政客、美利坚合众国总统的一时兴起，

sentences.en: as he is seeking retribution,
sentences.zh: 当他在寻求报复时，

sentences.en: it's using the government in a way that starts to chill a lot of democratic behavior.
sentences.zh: 这种政府的使用方式开始压制大量的民主行为。

sentences.en: It changes the entire relationship between the government and the people it governs.
sentences.zh: 它改变了政府与其所治理的人民之间的整个关系。

sentences.en: And how could it not?
sentences.zh: 怎么可能不改变呢？

sentences.en: When retribution is the central tool that a president is using to govern,
sentences.zh: 当复仇成为总统治理的核心工具时，

sentences.en: what will anyone else in the system be willing to do?
sentences.zh: 体制内的其他人还愿意做些什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: How far will they be willing to stick out their neck?
sentences.zh: 他们愿意冒多大的险？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: So given those obviously very high stakes you just outlined, I want you to take us inside this reporting you did
sentences.zh: 因此，鉴于你刚刚概述的那些显而易见的高风险，我想带我们深入了解你所做的这篇报道，

sentences.en: into what this campaign of retribution by Trump actually looked like in the first term so that we can understand what it's very likely to look like in a second term.
sentences.zh: 即特朗普在第一任期内的这场复仇行动实际上是什么样子的，以便我们能够理解它在第二任期内很可能会是什么样子。

sentences.en: There's been some intrigue surrounding the former secretary of state this weekend.
sentences.zh: 这个周末，前国务卿周围流传着一些阴谋传闻。

sentences.en: So the story starts on the campaign trail in 2016.
sentences.zh: 所以故事要从2016年的竞选活动说起。

sentences.en: She was questioned by the FBI Saturday about her use of a private email server while she was in the Obama administration.
sentences.zh: 周六，她因在奥巴马政府期间使用私人电子邮件服务器一事接受了联邦调查局的质询。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton was under investigation for her use of a personal email account.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿因使用个人电子邮件账户而接受调查。

sentences.en: We cannot find a case that would support bringing criminal charges on these facts.
sentences.zh: 我们找不到支持根据这些事实提起刑事指控的案件。

sentences.en: But the FBI announces there's just not enough evidence to bring criminal charges.
sentences.zh: 但联邦调查局宣布，没有足够的证据来提起刑事指控。

sentences.en: We are going to investigate this phony investigation.
sentences.zh: 我们要调查这场虚假的调查。

sentences.en: And not only was Donald Trump angry that she wasn't prosecuted...
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普不仅对她没有被起诉感到愤怒……

sentences.en: She deleted the emails.
sentences.zh: 她删除了邮件。

sentences.en: She has to go to jail.
sentences.zh: 她必须进监狱。

sentences.en: He was vowing that if he won, that he would lock her up.
sentences.zh: 他发誓如果他赢了，他就会把她关起来。

sentences.en: Lock her up is right.
sentences.zh: “把她关起来”确实没错。

sentences.en: But after Trump won, the first major thing he did was he came to the New York Times for an interview.
sentences.zh: 但在特朗普获胜后，他做的第一件大事就是来到《纽约时报》接受采访。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I was in the room for it.
sentences.zh: 我当时就在房间里。

sentences.en: Mr. President, thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，感谢您莅临。

sentences.en: In that interview, Trump seemingly backed away from this idea.
sentences.zh: 在那次采访中，特朗普似乎从这个想法中退缩了。

sentences.en: No, I want to bring the country together, James.
sentences.zh: 不，我想把这个国家凝聚在一起，詹姆斯。

sentences.en: It's very important.
sentences.zh: 这非常重要。

sentences.en: And he's asked, what is he going to do about Hillary Clinton?
sentences.zh: 当被问及他打算如何处理希拉里·克林顿的事情时，

sentences.en: And he signals that he essentially has little interest in trying to prosecute her.
sentences.zh: 他暗示自己基本上没有兴趣试图起诉她。

sentences.en: I don't want to hurt the Clintons.
sentences.zh: 我不想伤害克林顿一家。

sentences.en: I really don't.
sentences.zh: 我真的不想。

sentences.en: I don't want to hurt the Clintons, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不想伤害克林顿一家。

sentences.en: For everyone who heard that, the message was,
sentences.zh: 对于听到这话的每个人来说，传达的信息都是，

sentences.en: I'm not going to try and prosecute her.
sentences.zh: 我不会试图去起诉她。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Bear the hatchet.
sentences.zh: 化干戈为玉帛。

sentences.en: Enough's enough.
sentences.zh: 够了就够了。

sentences.en: And there's sort of a sigh of relief within Trump's inner circle that, okay, when he comes to Washington,
sentences.zh: 特朗普核心圈子里的人都松了一口气，心想，好吧，当他来到华盛顿后，

sentences.en: he's not going to be concentrated on trying to weaponize the criminal powers of the government against his enemies.
sentences.zh: 他不会全神贯注于试图将政府的刑事权力武器化来对付他的政敌。

sentences.en: But as Trump's administration begins, he finds himself and his campaign under investigation for their ties to Russia.
sentences.zh: 但随着特朗普政府的开始，他发现自己和他的竞选团队因与俄罗斯的联系而遭到调查。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this casts a massive shadow over his presidency and almost paralyzes him.
sentences.zh: 这给他的总统任期投下了巨大的阴影，几乎使他陷入瘫痪。

sentences.en: And by the beginning of his second year in office, as those investigations into him are accelerating, a light bulb of sorts goes off in his head.
sentences.zh: 到了他上任的第二年年初，随着对他的调查不断加速，他的脑海里闪现出一个类似灯泡的灵感。

sentences.en: And he basically says to his aides, damn it, if I'm being investigated by my own government, why can't I have the government investigate my enemies?
sentences.zh: 他基本上对他的助手说，妈的，如果我正受到自己政府的调查，为什么我不能让政府去调查我的敌人？

sentences.en: He understands what I like to call the specter of criminality and what that has done to him.
sentences.zh: 他理解我喜欢称之为犯罪阴影的东西，以及这对他的影响。

sentences.en: And he wants to turn that around and go on the offense.
sentences.zh: 他想要扭转局面，转入进攻。

sentences.en: And so what does he do?
sentences.zh: 那么他是怎么做的呢？

sentences.en: One of the first people who he starts musing about having investigated is the former FBI director, James Comey.
sentences.zh: 他开始盘算着要调查的第一批人之一就是前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米。

sentences.en: Comey had been the one who held the press conference to announce that the FBI didn't think there was a criminal case to be made against Hillary Clinton for her use of a private email account.
sentences.zh: 科米曾召开新闻发布会宣布联邦调查局认为没有理由就希拉里·克林顿使用私人电子邮件账户一事提起刑事诉讼。

sentences.en: After Trump became president, he tried to get Comey to pledge his loyalty to him.
sentences.zh: 特朗普成为总统后，曾试图让科米向他宣誓效忠。

sentences.en: And then Comey was leading investigations into ties between the people around Trump and Russia.
sentences.zh: 然后科米领导了对特朗普身边人与俄罗斯之间联系的调查。

sentences.en: And Trump had fired him early in his presidency.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在他总统任期初就解雇了他。

sentences.en: And in the aftermath of that, Comey had had memos disclosed about his interactions with Trump that helped lead to the appointment of a special counsel.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，科米披露了关于他与特朗普互动的备忘录，这促成了特别检察官的任命。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Trump had a lot of reasons not to like James Comey.
sentences.zh: 所以特朗普有很多理由不喜欢詹姆斯·科米。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: And Trump starts telling his White House chief of staff, John Kelly, that he wants to use the IRS and its unique investigative powers to go after Comey,
sentences.zh: 特朗普开始告诉他的白宫办公厅主任约翰·凯利，他想利用国税局及其独特的调查权力去对付科米、

sentences.en: Comey's deputy and other top FBI officials who were part of the Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 科米的副手以及参与俄罗斯调查的其他高级联邦调查局官员。

sentences.en: And I know from my own reporting that to Kelly, a four star Marine general, this was an awful thing for a president to be considering.
sentences.zh: 我从我自己的报道中得知，对于四星海军陆战队将军凯利来说，这是总统正在考虑的一件糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Kelly saw it as something right out of an authoritarian's playbook.
sentences.zh: 凯利认为这简直是独裁者惯用的伎俩。

sentences.en: And so Kelly essentially told Trump, I'm not going along with this.
sentences.zh: 所以凯利基本上告诉特朗普，我不会随你一起胡闹。

sentences.en: This is a terrible idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: You can't do this.
sentences.zh: 你不能这么做。

sentences.en: But Trump refuses to give up.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普拒绝放弃。

sentences.en: He wanted to find a way to get back at his enemies.
sentences.zh: 他想找个方法来报复他的敌人。

sentences.en: And he starts to muse about a different idea.
sentences.zh: 他开始盘算一个不同的主意。

sentences.en: He tells his White House counsel, Don McGahn, that he wants to try and use the Justice Department to go after Comey.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他的白宫法律顾问唐·麦加恩，他想试图利用司法部去对付科米。

sentences.en: And not just Comey.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是科米。

sentences.en: Also, his old foe, Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 还有他的老对手希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: So he's kind of graduating from just the idea of the IRS going after Comey.
sentences.zh: 所以他从仅仅让国税局对付科米的想法，升级了。

sentences.en: Now it's the Justice Department maybe going after Comey and Clinton.
sentences.zh: 现在可能是司法部去对付科米和克林顿。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: And if the Justice Department won't do that, Trump says, he himself wants to go and prosecute them.
sentences.zh: 如果司法部不这样做，特朗普说，他自己要亲自去起诉他们。

sentences.en: What does that even mean?
sentences.zh: 这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Because the president is not a legal officer in the administration.
sentences.zh: 因为总统并不是政府中的法律官员。

sentences.en: The whole problem with this is that it fell into this unique crack that Kelly and McGahn often found themselves in with Trump.
sentences.zh: 这里全部的问题在于，它落入了凯利和麦加恩经常在特朗普身上发现的那种独特的盲区。

sentences.en: When Trump wanted to do something that he didn't have the power to do, Kelly would say, look, you got to go to Congress and get them to pass a law or you can't do it.

sentences.en: Trump would usually give up and go away.

sentences.en: But just to explain, Trump as president did have some powers to direct the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 但需要解释一下的是，特朗普作为总统确实拥有一些权力来直接指挥司法部。

sentences.en: It's part of the executive branch.

sentences.en: The president can tell the Justice Department how to execute the law.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Plus, he appoints the people who lead it.

sentences.en: But there's a longstanding norm that this is something presidents should not do.
sentences.zh: 但长期以来一直有一个规范，即总统不应该这样做。

sentences.en: And that's because of Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 而这正是因为理查德·尼克松。

sentences.en: When Richard Nixon was president, he tried to use the powers of the federal government against his enemies.
sentences.zh: 当理查德·尼克松担任总统时，他试图利用联邦政府的权力来对付政敌。

sentences.en: And after Nixon resigned over abuses of his power, there was a norm that took hold.
sentences.zh: 在尼克松因滥用职权辞职后，形成了一种惯例。

sentences.en: Which is what?

sentences.en: That presidents should have nothing to do with telling the Justice Department or the FBI or the IRS how to use their vast investigative powers.
sentences.zh: 即总统不应干涉司法部、联邦调查局或国税局如何利用其庞大的调查权力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So kind of an unwritten rule.

sentences.en: But Trump didn't care about that.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普根本不在乎这一点。

sentences.en: But he didn't care about post-Watergate norms and where the line between the Justice Department and the White House begins and ends.

sentences.en: He wanted to go after his enemies.

sentences.en: And he asked about doing it so often that Kelly and McGahn came up with their own sort of playbook on how to deal with this.
sentences.zh: 他频繁询问如何下手，以至于凯利和麦加恩不得不制定了一套应对这种局面的方案。

sentences.en: And that was to write Trump a memo.

sentences.en: And what McGahn was doing was finding a way to bide some time until Trump would become distracted with something else,

sentences.en: but also create a written record about the counsel that was being given to the president.

sentences.en: And so McGahn turns around to lawyers in the White House counsel's office and asked them to write a memo about what Trump's powers are to direct the Justice Department and whether that is a good idea or not.

sentences.en: But under the terms that the person allowed me to see them, I couldn't take them with me and I couldn't take copies.

sentences.en: But here we have very clear evidence of how Donald Trump has effectively weaponized his Department of Justice against his enemies,
sentences.zh: 但在这里，我们有了非常明确的证据，表明唐纳德·特朗普如何有效地将他的司法部武器化来对付政敌，

sentences.en: because what you're describing is two United States Attorney's offices, their staff, spending more than a year investigating whether or not Trump's enemy, John Kerry,
sentences.zh: 因为你所描述的是两个美国联邦检察官办公室及其工作人员，花费了超过一年的时间来调查特朗普的政敌约翰·克里

sentences.en: did something illegal.
sentences.zh: 是否做过违法的事。

sentences.en: And as best we can tell, that came at the suggestion of Donald Trump himself.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，这正是唐纳德·特朗普本人建议的产物。

sentences.en: I like to describe it as this unique use of presidential power, where through public calls and private pressure and fears that Trump will fire his attorney general or lash out,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把它描述为总统权力的这种独特运用：通过公开呼吁、私下施压，以及利用特朗普会解雇司法部长或大发雷霆的恐惧，

sentences.en: that the Justice Department goes along and does the political errands of the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 司法部随波逐流，去替美国总统跑政治腿。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In this case, though, political errands that involve the prosecutorial powers of the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，跑的政治腿却涉及司法部的起诉权。

sentences.en: The criminal powers of the government.
sentences.zh: 政府的刑事权力。

sentences.en: You said in the end there are something like a dozen instances where this happens.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说，最终发生类似情况的实例大约有十几次。

sentences.en: Help us understand some of the others beyond this one case, John Kerry.
sentences.zh: 请帮我们了解除了约翰·克里这个案子之外的其他一些情况。

sentences.en: John Bolton, Trump's former national security advisor, wrote a embarrassing book about Trump.
sentences.zh: 约翰·博尔顿，特朗普的前国家安全顾问，写了一本让特朗普尴尬的书。

sentences.en: The Justice Department went to court to try and stop the publication of the book, to recoup the profits that Bolton made from it,
sentences.zh: 司法部诉诸法院，试图阻止该书的出版，以追回博尔顿从中获得的利润，

sentences.en: and also opened a criminal investigation into whether he mishandled classified information, all as Trump was demanding that the book not come out.
sentences.zh: 同时还对他就涉嫌处理机密信息不当展开了刑事调查，而这一切正值特朗普要求该书不得出版之际。

sentences.en: Well, well, what about the original targets of all his fury, like Hillary Clinton and James Comey?
sentences.zh: 那么，他所有愤怒的最初目标呢，比如希拉里·克林顿和詹姆斯·科米？

sentences.en: Well, when it comes to Comey, remember, Trump wanted not only the IRS to investigate him, but also the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 嗯，说到科米，你要知道，特朗普不仅想让国税局调查他，还想让司法部调查他。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The thing that Trump wanted Comey investigated for was being a leaker.
sentences.zh: 特朗普想要调查科米的原因是他是个泄密者。

sentences.en: Well, Comey did come under investigation for leaking classified information.
sentences.zh: 嗯，科米确实因涉嫌泄露机密信息而遭到调查。

sentences.en: Criminal investigation.
sentences.zh: 一项刑事调查。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: An investigation that cost him tens of thousands of dollars in legal fees and allowed federal investigators to go through some of his communications.
sentences.zh: 这项调查让他花费了数万美元的律师费，并允许联邦调查人员查阅他的一些通信记录。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And then there was what we learned about what the IRS did to Comey.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们要聊聊我们所了解到的美国国税局对科米做过的事。

sentences.en: What did the IRS do?
sentences.zh: 国税局做了什么？

sentences.en: The IRS has a special, unique type of audit that is called by accountants, an autopsy without the benefit of death.
sentences.zh: 国税局有一种极其特殊、独一无二的审计，被会计师们称为“死前解剖”。

sentences.en: It's incredibly invasive.
sentences.zh: 这具有极强的侵入性。

sentences.en: It essentially looks at your entire year of finances, everything you spent money on, every charitable donation you made, every exemption you claimed,
sentences.zh: 它基本上会审查你一整年的财务状况、你花的每一笔钱、你做过的每一笔慈善捐款、你申请过的每一项减免，

sentences.en: and sees whether you properly paid your taxes.
sentences.zh: 以此来检查你是否足额纳税。

sentences.en: Sounds extremely unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 听起来极其糟糕。

sentences.en: It is done to just a few thousand people a year.
sentences.zh: 每年只有几千人会遭遇这种审计。

sentences.en: What I learned was that James Comey and his deputy at the FBI, Andrew McCabe, who Trump also wanted to go after, were both the subject of this highly unusual and invasive audit.
sentences.zh: 我了解到的是，詹姆斯·科米和他在联邦调查局的副局长安德鲁·麦凯布——这也是特朗普一直想对付的人——都成了这项高度异常且极具侵入性审计的目标。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That doesn't seem like a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 这看起来可不像是巧合。

sentences.en: In fact, based on our number crunchers here, the chances that they would both be chosen are one in 82 million.
sentences.zh: 事实上，根据我们这里的数据专家的计算，他们两人同时被选中的几率是八千二百万分之一。

sentences.en: In other words, a more logical explanation is that President Trump asked for this to happen, and it did, or,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，更合乎逻辑的解释是，特朗普总统要求这件事发生，于是它就发生了，或者说，

sentences.en: as in the relationship between his tweets and the Department of Justice, that someone figured, well, Trump wants this, I'll do it for him.
sentences.zh: 就像他的推文与司法部的关系一样，有人心领神会地觉得，好吧，特朗普想要这个，那我就为他效劳。

sentences.en: Or it just happened.
sentences.zh: 或者它纯粹是个巧合。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We should point out here that the IRS inspector general went back and looked at this and has cleared the agency of any wrongdoing.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里应该指出，国税局督察长后来对此进行了调查，并宣布该机构没有违规行为。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What do Comey and his deputy, McCabe, have to say about all this?
sentences.zh: 对于这一切，科米和他的副手麦凯布怎么说？

sentences.en: It's very hard for both of them to accept at face value that this is random.
sentences.zh: 他们两人都很难相信这一切纯属巧合。

sentences.en: And this part of the story has one of the great chef's kisses of all time.
sentences.zh: 而故事的这一部分堪称神来之笔。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: After looking at all of James Comey's finances for the year of 2017, they found that he overpaid on his taxes, and he received a refund.
sentences.zh: 在查阅了詹姆斯·科米2017年全年的财务状况后，他们发现他税交多了，并给他退了款。

sentences.en: So in the end, Comey's not charged with a crime.
sentences.zh: 所以到头来，科米并没有被指控犯罪。

sentences.en: In fact, what he does is the opposite of a crime.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的做法与犯罪恰恰相反。

sentences.en: He gives the government too much money.
sentences.zh: 他给政府交了太多的钱。

sentences.en: I'm curious, what ends up happening with Hillary Clinton, the person we started this conversation with?
sentences.zh: 我很想知道，希拉里·克林顿最终怎么样了？也就是我们这场谈话最初提到的人。

sentences.en: At the suggestion of Trump's political appointees at the Justice Department,
sentences.zh: 在特朗普司法部政治任命官员的建议下，

sentences.en: a prosecutor is appointed who looks at a range of different conspiracy theories about Clinton and her 2016 campaign.
sentences.zh: 指派了一名检察官，负责调查关于克林顿及其2016年竞选团队的各种阴谋论。

sentences.en: That investigation becomes so vast that Clinton herself ultimately sits for questioning with prosecutors, a situation that if she had made a false statement in,
sentences.zh: 这项调查范围之广，以至于克林顿本人最终不得不接受检察官的讯问，如果在这种情况下她做出了虚假陈述，

sentences.en: she could have been charged.
sentences.zh: 她就会被起诉。

sentences.en: Right, but she wasn't charged.
sentences.zh: 对，但她并没有被起诉。

sentences.en: And in fact, as best I can tell, nobody we're talking about here, from Hillary Clinton to John Kerry to James Comey or Andrew McCabe,
sentences.zh: 事实上，据我所知，我们在这里谈论的任何人，从希拉里·克林顿到约翰·克里，再到詹姆斯·科米或安德鲁·麦凯布，

sentences.en: none of them were ultimately charged in these investigations that Trump wanted into his enemies.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普想要针对其政敌的这些调查中，他们最终都没有一个人遭到起诉。

sentences.en: So what should we make of that fact?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何看待这一事实呢？

sentences.en: And what does that tell us about, at the end of the day, how successful Trump's pursuit of his enemies really was?
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这说明了特朗普对政敌的追查究竟取得了多大的成功？

sentences.en: On one hand, you could say, wow, look, the three branches of government are holding up.
sentences.zh: 一方面，你可能会说，哇，你看，政府的三权分立还在坚守。

sentences.en: The Justice Department investigated something.
sentences.zh: 司法部调查了某些事情。

sentences.en: They knew if they went to indict someone, they'd have to go to court before a judge and ultimately never did that because they didn't have enough to get over that line.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，如果要去起诉某人，他们必须在法官面前出庭，而他们最终没有这样做，是因为他们没有足够的证据跨过那条线。

sentences.en: On the other hand, I'm not sure whether these people being indicted is where we should measure whether this was a success or not for Trump.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我不确定这些人是否被起诉，是我们衡量这对特朗普来说是否成功标准。

sentences.en: Because these people came under investigation.
sentences.zh: 因为这些人确实受到了调查。

sentences.en: They knew that they were under investigation.
sentences.zh: 他们知道自己正在接受调查。

sentences.en: A prosecutor once said to me, you can ruin someone's life by just investigating them.
sentences.zh: 一位检察官曾对我说，仅仅是调查就能毁掉一个人的一生。

sentences.en: It's anxiety-inducing for the subject of the investigation and for their families.
sentences.zh: 这会给调查对象及其家人带来极大的焦虑。

sentences.en: In some cases, it can cost hundreds of thousands of dollars.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，这会花费几十万美元。

sentences.en: The government can gain access to a wide array of your communications and financial information.
sentences.zh: 政府可以获取你广泛的通讯记录和财务信息。

sentences.en: It's not nothing.
sentences.zh: 这可不是小事。

sentences.en: So if you're Trump and your original goal was to seek retribution against your enemies, you're saying the fact that there are no charges doesn't mean he failed.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是特朗普，你最初的目标是对政敌进行报复，那你就会认为，没有提出指控并不意味着他失败了。

sentences.en: The investigations themselves are, in many ways, the revenge and the retribution.
sentences.zh: 调查本身在许多方面就是一种复仇和报复。

sentences.en: Whether or not Trump sees it that way, the reality is, is that for the people that were subjects of these investigations,
sentences.zh: 不管特朗普是否这样看待，现实情况是，对于那些成为这些调查对象的人来说，

sentences.en: these were awful experiences that felt to them like retribution.
sentences.zh: 这些都是可怕的经历，对他们来说就像是报复。

sentences.en: They felt like the vast powers of the federal government were being used against them punitively.
sentences.zh: 他们感觉联邦政府的庞大权力正在被用来惩罚他们。

sentences.en: So, Mike, now that you've so clearly established how far Trump's desire for retribution went in the first term, the degree to which it wasn't hypothetical bluster,
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克，既然你已经清楚地阐明了特朗普在第一任期内对报复的渴望达到了何种程度，这种渴望并非假设性的虚张声势，

sentences.en: but became punitive, painful reality for the Boltons and the Clintons and the Comeys of the world.
sentences.zh: 而是变成了博尔顿、克林顿和科米之流痛苦而现实的惩罚。

sentences.en: How do you think about what form this is going to take in a second Trump term?
sentences.zh: 你认为如果特朗普迎来第二个任期，这种形式会变成什么样？

sentences.en: What I have laid out is what happened when you had figures like John Kelly and Don McGahn in the room trying to protect the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 我刚才陈述的是，当约翰·凯利和唐·麦加恩这样的人物在房间里试图捍卫法治时发生的事情。

sentences.en: The people who consider themselves the adults in the room.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些自认为是房间里的成年人的人。

sentences.en: Trump has made clear that those types of guardrails will be turned into enablers if he returns to the White House.
sentences.zh: 特朗普已经明确表示，如果他重返白宫，那些护栏将会变成帮凶。

sentences.en: You don't need to have such an imagination to see what those factors taken together will look like if Trump, who's been indicted four times since he left the White House,
sentences.zh: 如果特朗普在离开白宫后已经被起诉了四次，

sentences.en: will do with the criminal powers of the government if he gets back into power.
sentences.zh: 那么当他重新掌权后，利用政府的刑事权力会做出什么事，我们不需要太多的想象力就能看清这些因素结合在一起会是什么样子。

sentences.en: You're raising an interesting possibility here, which is there's not just fewer guardrails and more enablers.
sentences.zh: 你在这里提出了一个有趣的可能，那就是不仅护栏变少了，帮凶变多了。

sentences.en: There's more vindictiveness.
sentences.zh: 而且报复心更强了。

sentences.en: There's more targets of his desire for retribution because since that first term, there have been more investigations against him, more charges against him.
sentences.zh: 他渴望报复的目标更多了，因为自第一任期以来，针对他的调查更多了，对他的指控也更多了。

sentences.en: This thing that, as you once said in this conversation, the light bulb went off in his head and he understood he could inflict on his enemies.
sentences.zh: 正如你在这场谈话中曾经说过的那样，他脑子里灵光一闪，意识到自己可以给政敌带来痛苦。

sentences.en: There are more of those enemies now.
sentences.zh: 现在这样的政敌更多了。

sentences.en: There are more targets.
sentences.zh: 目标更多了。

sentences.en: We know he did it in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他过去这么干过。

sentences.en: We know he's saying he'll do it if he comes back.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他说过如果回来还会这么干。

sentences.en: And I think we need to reckon with what the consequences of such a far-reaching culture of retribution would mean to the country.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须认真面对这种影响深远的报复文化会给国家带来什么后果。

sentences.en: If you're a Democrat on Capitol Hill and you think you should conduct an oversight investigation into the president, are you going to think twice about it?
sentences.zh: 如果你是国会山的一名民主党人，并且认为你应该对总统进行监督调查，你还会三思而后行吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Are you going to get investigated?
sentences.zh: 你会不会遭到调查？

sentences.en: If you are a member of Trump's party and you want to speak out against something that he's doing, are you going to think twice about it?
sentences.zh: 如果你是特朗普所在党派的成员，并且想公开反对他正在做的事情，你还会三思而后行吗？

sentences.en: If you're an activist and you want to have a protest outside the White House, are you going to take that risk?
sentences.zh: 如果你是一名活动人士，想在白宫外举行抗议活动，你还会冒这个险吗？

sentences.en: Trump has said he wants to prosecute election workers.
sentences.zh: 特朗普曾表示他想要起诉选举工作人员。

sentences.en: Those are everyday people.
sentences.zh: 那些都是普通人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Not just senior administration officials, not just Jim Comey.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是高级行政官员，不仅仅是吉姆·科米。

sentences.en: Not everyone is James Comey, who has the money to hire high-end criminal defense lawyers and is a well-established guy who can stand in the face of an investigation.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人都是詹姆斯·科米，他有钱聘请高端刑事辩护律师，而且是一位能够经受得住调查考验的知名人士。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what is the trickle-down effect to everyone else?
sentences.zh: 那么对其他所有人的涟漪效应是什么？

sentences.en: When Trump was president, my phone records were subpoenaed by the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 当特朗普担任总统时，我的通话记录被司法部传唤了。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Was that done because Donald Trump railed on and on about the media being the enemy of the people and saying they should be criminally investigated as part of leak investigations?
sentences.zh: 这是因为唐纳德·特朗普喋喋不休地抨击媒体是人民的敌人，并称作为泄密调查的一部分，应该对媒体进行刑事调查吗？

sentences.en: Or was it done because a prosecutor thought it was the right thing based on the evidence in the law as they tried to get to the bottom of how classified information became public?
sentences.zh: 还是因为检察官在试图弄清机密信息是如何公开的过程中，根据法律证据认为这是正确做法？

sentences.en: When the president of the United States is weighing in against people and saying that they should be investigated, as a citizen, how do you look at it and say,
sentences.zh: 当美国总统对人们指指点点并声称应该对他们进行调查时，作为一名公民，你怎么能看待并坚信，

sentences.en: okay, I can trust that that was done based on the law and the evidence?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我可以相信这是依法依规进行的？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The well becomes poisoned.
sentences.zh: 水源被污染了。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when you start to have those doubts, it begins to unravel the confidence that the public has in its government.
sentences.zh: 当你开始产生这些怀疑时，公众对政府的信任就会开始瓦解。

sentences.en: Well, Mike, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，迈克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们深表感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Hurricane Milton tore across Florida in the early hours of Thursday morning, ripping off the roof of the Tropicana Field, home of the Tampa Bay Rays baseball team,
sentences.zh: 飓风“米尔顿”在周四清晨肆虐佛罗里达州，掀开了坦帕湾光芒棒球队主场纯果乐球场的屋顶，

sentences.en: slamming a crane into a high-rise building in St. Petersburg and knocking out power to about a third of the state.
sentences.zh: 将一台起重机刮倒在圣彼得堡的一栋高层建筑上，并导致该州约三分之一的地区断电。

sentences.en: What we can say is the storm was significant, but thankfully, this was not the worst-case scenario.
sentences.zh: 我们可以说这场风暴规模很大，但谢天谢地，这并不是最坏的情况。

sentences.en: But overall, the storm was less lethal than expected.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，风暴的致命性低于预期。

sentences.en: The storm did weaken before landfall, and the storm surge, as initially reported, has not been as significant overall as what was observed for Hurricane Helene right now.
sentences.zh: 风暴在登陆前确实减弱了，而且正如最初报道的那样，风暴潮总体上并不像目前“海伦”飓风所观测到的那么严重。

sentences.en: As of Thursday night, at least 12 people were killed by the storm, several from a series of tornadoes that touched down on Florida's East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 截至周四晚间，这场风暴已造成至少12人死亡，其中几人死于登陆佛罗里达州东海岸的一系列龙卷风。

sentences.en: Remember, you can listen to a new episode of The Interview right here tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你明天就可以在这里收听《访谈》的新一期节目。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko and Mary Wilson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科和玛丽·威尔逊制作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱有时甚至扣人心弦的权力斗争中。
